name: Dorestad
about: The first river place: Dorestad at the fork of the Kromme Rijn and the Lek, c. 800, at true size
centre_about: RD New: between the fork and the Hoogstraat

rivers.name: Lek
rivers.about: the 800 Lek: the Vos 800 AD map's inland water; 4.5 m at mid-river

rivers.name: Kromme Rijn
rivers.about: the 800 Kromme Rijn: nl_793's class 3, cut along the Vos line; 2.8 m at mid-river

water_level.about: low on the banks, so the levees and most banks stand over it: p20 of the ground 10-60 m from the water

settlement.about: the ribbon settlement along the Kromme Rijn from the fork, its clearing wide on the town's (west) bank and a landing strip on the far bank (guesses: ED4 ch. V 3, ch. VIII 1.1)

clearings.label: De Geer's clearing
clearings.about: the De Geer farms, c. 500 m west of the harbour on an older levee (JALC 2010; a guess)

clearings.label: Rijswijk's clearing (the villa and the lost castellum south of the Lek)
clearings.about: level metres; the fort's site is lost to the river (ED4 ch. VIII; a guess)

sources: The Netherlands c. 800 from AHN4 lidar (CC0), the first build's Bake/realground/nl_793.py
Vos et al., paleogeographic map 800 AD (inland water: the 800 Lek; veen: the Langbroek peat)
Cohen et al. 2012, Rhine-Meuse delta channel belts (CC BY 4.0), via the 800 channel; active belts c. 800 and the dead sandy ridges
Van der Tuuk, Dorestad onthuld ch. 2; Gouw-Bouman 2025 Veget Hist Archaeobot 34; Van Es & Verwers 2015 (NO 18) ch. VIII: what grew where
